title: EVICPRESS: Joint KV-Cache Compression and Eviction for Efficient LLM Serving
why_it_matters: Reusing key-value (KV) caches is crucial for fast LLM inference, but GPU memory fills up quickly as contexts and user counts grow. Existing approaches either evict caches to slower storage tiers using simple rules like LRU or compress caches in GPU memory independently, leading to suboptimal tradeoffs between latency and text quality. EVICPRESS jointly optimizes eviction and compression decisions across all contexts by recognizing that different contexts have varying sensitivities to compression errors. For software engineers building LLM serving infrastructure, this approach provides significantly faster time-to-first-token while maintaining output quality, allowing systems to serve more context efficiently on multi-tier storage hardware.
problem_statement: Existing LLM serving systems treat KV-cache eviction to lower-tier storage and KV-cache compression as isolated optimizations. This misses the opportunity to globally manage cache placement and compression ratios based on each context's unique sensitivity to quality loss.
method: Jointly optimizes lossy compression and adaptive eviction decisions across multiple storage tiers rather than treating them separately.
Uses a unified utility function to quantify the overall impact of lossy compression and eviction choices on generation quality and latency.
Employs a profiling module that periodically updates utility function scores across possible eviction and compression configurations for all contexts.
Adapts compression methods (e.g., keydiff, knorm, snapkv) and ratios on a per-context basis because error sensitivity does not correlate simply with context length or domain type.
Applies a fast heuristic to rearrange KV caches across storage tiers to maximize overall utility scores on each tier.
key_results: Achieves up to 2.19x faster time-to-first-token (TTFT) at equivalent generation quality compared to separate compression or eviction baselines.
Reduces TTFT by 1.43x to 3.77x at equal quality compared to compression combined with LRU-based eviction.
Reduces TTFT by 1.22x to 1.56x compared to prefill and eviction-only schemes.
Demonstrates that optimal compression methods and ratios vary widely across contexts, with no single compression method dominating.
limitations: Inferred: The periodic profiling module introduces additional computational overhead by generating utility scores on training queries before or during operation.
Inferred: Experiments were evaluated on a single 80GB H100 GPU with fixed storage bandwidth assumptions, leaving performance on multi-GPU or distributed environments unverified in the text.
Inferred: Training and evaluation relied on synthetic queries generated by GPT-5 rather than live production workload traces.
followup_questions: What is the runtime overhead and memory footprint of the profiling module during high-throughput production serving?
How well does the global joint-optimization heuristic scale when handling tens of thousands of concurrent active contexts?
How does EVICPRESS adapt when user context sensitivities or query patterns shift dynamically during runtime?
confidence_notes: Note that the text refers to the system as 'EVICPRESS' in most sections, but refers to it as 'CacheServe' in the conclusion section. The briefing treats them as referencing the same system described in the paper.
